entries.proposition: Design: a cross-sectional study with a longitudinal follow-up, parents recruited through a foundation, repeat assessments at 6 and 12 months.
entries.snippet: The study protocol called for a repeat of the COAs at 6 and 12 months with follow-up continuing through February 2023.

entries.proposition: Test-retest reliability was assessed by asking parents to repeat selected forms about two weeks later, only some forms per parent.
entries.snippet: To assess test-retest reliability, parents were also assigned to complete COAs at approximately 2 weeks after completing them for a study time point.

entries.proposition: Of 65 participants, 55 completed all or almost all assessments over the year; 5 dropped out after baseline and 1 child died.
entries.snippet: The remaining 55 completed all or almost all the planned assessments over the course of a year.

entries.proposition: The median Vineland-3 composite standardized score was 34, about 4.4 standard deviations below the norm mean; most communication standardized scores sat at the floor.
entries.snippet: The median Vineland-3 composite standardized score was 34 (IQR 26–46, max = 74).

entries.proposition: Floor effects grow with age: expressive communication floor values rose from 25 percent at 12 to 23 months to 81, 96 and 94 percent at 2 to 4, 5 to 9 and 10 or more years.
entries.snippet: while 25% of those aged 12–23 months had floor values for expressive communication, this rose to 81%, 96%, and 94% in those aged 2–4, 5–9, and 10 years and older

entries.proposition: Untreated change over about a year: the standardized composite fell by 2.8 points per year (p 0.002) and the communication standardized score by 2.6; none of the other scores changed substantially.
entries.snippet: The Vineland ABC and communication-standardized scores demonstrated significant declines, −2.8 ( p = 0.002) and −2.6 ( p = 0.01) points per year, respectively.

entries.proposition: Growth scale values changed little in a year: receptive minus 1.5 (interval minus 4.32 to 1.33) and expressive plus 0.3 (interval minus 1.11 to 1.72); the intervals include zero, and bound the cohort mean change.
entries.snippet: The estimated change in the GSVs over the course of 1 year was −1.5 (95% CI −4.32 to 1.33) for receptive communication and 0.3 (95% CI −1.11 to 1.72) for expressive communication.

entries.proposition: All test-retest intraclass correlations were above 0.90, including the Vineland standardized and growth scale values.
entries.snippet: All ICCs were >0.90 for all measures including Vineland standardized and GSV scores, indicating excellent test-retest validity

entries.proposition: Convergence: growth scale values correlated at 0.7 to 0.9 with the raw-score communication instruments but mostly below 0.5 with the Vineland standardized scores.
entries.snippet: Correlations were mostly <0.5 with several below 0.3 for Vineland standardized scores with other scores, including the Vineland GSVs.

entries.proposition: The authors state that knowing the likely magnitude and variability of change without treatment is critical for planning a trial, and report no substantial untreated change in the non-standardised scores over a year.
entries.snippet: As in the BUTTERFLY study, 46 we found no substantial change over the course of a year in any of the nonstandardized scores.

entries.proposition: The authors infer, but do not demonstrate, sensitivity to within-patient change from cross-sectional discrimination; they state growth scale values lack a normative reference and acceptance by the regulator is pending.
entries.snippet: From this, we can infer, if not directly demonstrate, likely sensitivity to within-patient changes over time should they occur in the context of a trial.

entries.proposition: Limitations stated: convenience sample recruited through a foundation (possible skew to severe), parent-report only, convergence with clinician assessment not yet shown in severely impaired populations.
entries.snippet: Such convergence still needs to be demonstrated specifically in severely impaired populations.

entries.proposition: Cannabidiol trials using the standardized score may have been null in part because of floor effects, according to the authors, despite parents seeing meaningful non-seizure benefits.
entries.snippet: may have contributed to the null findings for the Vineland in the cannabidiol trials

Figure 1 shows, for six communication milestones, the shares of children in four age groups reported as not having, learning or having mastered each; the bar for 'Tells a story (5 years)' is almost entirely 'No' in every age group.
